cover.headline: A world-class chemistry franchise priced ahead of its pipeline: the history supports ~59x earnings, and that is below today's price
cover.lead: Divi's Laboratories is India's largest maker of active pharmaceutical ingredients (APIs) and one of the world's ten largest small-molecule contract manufacturers. Of FY26 revenue of ₹10,560 cr, 55% was custom synthesis for big pharma, 36% generic APIs and 9% nutraceuticals. Q1FY27 was exceptional: revenue +28% (only ~10% in constant currency), EBITDA margin 40.7%, as validation batches of three dedicated projects (~₹2,000 cr of capex) shipped and the rupee slumped. The stock rose from ~₹6,700 in June to ₹9,292 on 30-Sep-2026, above the ₹9,106 median of the post-results targets. The street values Divi's on **P/E** (Motilal Oswal 55x 12-month forward, BOBCAPS 56x Mar-28E) or EV/EBITDA (JM 41x, HDFC 39x). We forecast EPS of ₹118.0 / ₹137.0 / ₹158.0 for FY27-29E, ~5-10% below the post-results street. Divi's own one-year-forward P/E median since 2021 (55.9x) times the pharma sector factor (×1.0545) gives **59x Sep-28E EPS of ₹147.5 = {{dcf.tp|inr}} ({{dcf.upside|chg}}): we initiate with SELL**. Cross-checks: EV/EBITDA ₹8,817, DCF ₹2,872. Bull case {{scen.bull.tp|inr}}; bear case {{scen.bear.tp|inr}}.

arguments.p: Divi's works for 12 of the world's 20 largest drug makers, 18-20 of its projects are commercial or being commercialised, and customers prepaid ₹1,207 cr in FY26 to reserve capacity. It is the largest maker of ten generic APIs, backward-integrated through a new plant at Kakinada, and has had clean USFDA outcomes since 2017. Few Indian companies can claim this; we do not dispute the quality.

arguments.h: The growth the price needs is not yet visible
arguments.p: Constant-currency growth was 6.8% in FY26 and ~10% in Q1FY27. The three dedicated projects are validated, but commercial volumes wait for customers' regulatory approvals ("by 2027"; the first was once targeted for Jan-2027). Peptide and GLP-1 work is promising and undisclosed. We already model custom synthesis +26.5% / +22.2% / +18.4% (to 64% of sales by FY29E).

arguments.h: Q1FY27 is not the new run-rate
arguments.p: The 68% gross margin came with a ~₹500 cr inventory build (a three-month raw-material stockpile at war-inflated solvent prices, plus validation work in progress). Management says the gross margin will not hold at that level and FY27's EBITDA margin will be 'similar' to FY26's 32.6%. We model 35.5% for FY27E (Q2-Q4 ~34%), already giving credit for the weak rupee.

At ₹9,292 the stock trades at 78.7x our FY27E and 67.8x FY28E EPS. Our 59x target multiple is not stingy: it is Divi's own median since 2021 lifted ~5% for a sector that trades above its history, and it still sits below today's price. The DCF (₹2,872) says cash flows support far less. Below ~₹7,570 the rule would turn us buyers.

catalysts: Q2FY27 results (due by mid-November 2026): whether the gross margin stays near 60%+ as the stockpile is used, and whether custom synthesis holds ~60% of revenue without validation batches.
Customers' regulatory approvals for the three dedicated projects (management: commercialisation 'by 2027'); any SEBI disclosure of a new contract or the Kakinada Phase 2 (four blocks) decision.
The second iodine contrast-media long-term contract (expected within months of Aug-2026) and commercial volumes from four new generic DMFs (3-6 months).
The rupee and West Asia: a ceasefire would cut solvent costs but also remove part of the currency tailwind in rupee revenue.
US policy: Section 232 tariffs on patented APIs (live from 31-Jul / 29-Sep-2026) and the BIOSECURE Act, which may move work from Chinese CDMOs to India.

sections.title: One chemistry platform, three businesses: custom synthesis for big pharma, bulk generic APIs, and carotenoids

blocks.p: Divi's makes the active ingredients that go into other companies' medicines; it sells no finished drugs and competes with none of its customers. It runs three plants: Unit 1 near Hyderabad, Unit 2 near Visakhapatnam (which also houses the nutraceutical plant) and Unit 3 at Kakinada, which started in January 2025 and makes starting materials for the other two. About 89% of revenue is exported, 61% to Europe and 13% to North America (FY26). It employs ~19,300 people, ~700 of them scientists, and has ~18,600 KL of reactor capacity.

blocks.p: **Concentration is opaque.** Divi's names no customers or molecules ("we are bound by CDAs", confidentiality agreements). The only product data are life-cycle disclosures in the sustainability report: valsartan was 6.37% of standalone turnover in FY25 and 4.98% in FY26, naproxen 5.2% and 4.95%, levetiracetam 3.24%. Valsartan's fall is consistent with generic entry for Novartis's Entresto (sacubitril/valsartan) in the US in July 2025, a late-life-cycle custom product analysts link to Divi's; the CEO will not confirm any product but says Divi's routinely manages "late life cycle" volumes with its customers.

blocks.callout: **So what:** Divi's is not a generic company with a contract arm, nor a pure CDMO. It is a process-chemistry platform that uses the same plants, people and backward integration for both. That keeps costs low and lets capacity swing to whatever pays, but it also means investors cannot see the economics of any single contract, and must take the pipeline largely on trust.

sections.title: Thirty-six years of process chemistry, one regulatory scare, one windfall, and a founder still in charge

blocks.p: Dr. Murali K. Divi founded Divi's Research Centre in 1990 after co-founding Cheminor Drugs, which later merged into Dr. Reddy's. Divi's built its name making generic APIs at lower cost than anyone (by redesigning the chemistry and making its own starting materials) and doing contract work for innovators who valued its reliability. It listed in 2003 and issued 1:1 bonus shares in FY16; the share count (26.5 cr) has not changed since. The numbers fall into four eras.

blocks.callout: **Lesson from history:** Divi's has twice shown how fast its numbers move with a few large products: the 2017 import alert cut a year's growth, and Covid-era products lifted North America revenue to ₹3,833 cr in FY22 before it fell to ₹1,310 cr in FY24. The dedicated projects now coming on stream are the same kind of lumpy, customer-dependent revenue, which is why we do not extrapolate Q1FY27.

sections.title: Industry: outsourcing and peptides are growing fast; generic APIs are a price war; the war in West Asia raised costs and sank the rupee

blocks.p: **Contract manufacturing (CDMO) is the growth engine.** Drug companies increasingly outsource chemistry to specialists. The company quotes a global CDMO market of ~USD 150 bn (2024) heading to USD 290-300 bn by the early 2030s, with API CDMO the largest part (USD 107 bn to 210 bn by 2033), and BCG expects India's CRDMO sector to grow from USD 3-3.5 bn to 22-25 bn by 2035. Peptide medicines (led by GLP-1 drugs for diabetes and obesity) are ~USD 140 bn (2025) and could double by 2033; Macquarie sizes the peptide CDMO market at ~USD 4 bn in 2025 rising to USD 20-25 bn by 2030.

blocks.p: **Generic APIs are a price war.** Prices for large-volume APIs have fallen for two years as Chinese producers cut prices and insurers squeeze generic drug makers. Divi's says its volumes held and it lost no customers, but generic API revenue grew only ~1% in FY26 (PL's split) and ~6% in Q1FY27. China's withdrawal of export tax rebates on some chemicals from April 2026 raises input costs more than it helps Indian API makers. **The West Asia war (from 28-Feb-2026)** then doubled or tripled solvent prices, tightened methanol and ammonia supply and pushed freight up; it also sent the rupee to record lows (~95-97 per US dollar in May-June 2026), which lifts the rupee value of Divi's exports.

blocks.callout: **Our view:** the structural tailwinds (outsourcing, China+1, contrast media) reach Divi's directly and are visible in customer prepayments. The tailwinds the stock is most excited about, GLP-1 peptides and the dedicated projects, are real but not yet in the numbers, and the one most visible in Q1FY27 (the rupee) is the least durable.

sections.title: Custom synthesis: three paid-for projects are validated and waiting for their customers' approvals; peptides are the bigger, less certain prize

blocks.p: Custom synthesis (CS) revenue fell from ₹5,286 cr in FY22 (Covid products) to ₹3,418 cr in FY23, then rebuilt to ₹4,820 cr in FY25 and ₹5,808 cr in FY26 (+20%). In Q1FY27 it grew ~45% to ~₹1,848 cr, 60% of revenue, helped by validation batches of the three dedicated projects (HDFC Securities, PL) and the weak rupee. Divi's does three kinds of CS work: late-life-cycle supply of mature innovator APIs (where it takes over volume as patents near expiry), advanced intermediates and APIs for drugs still in their patent life, and newer platforms (peptide fragments, iodine and gadolinium contrast agents).

Since April 2024 Divi's has signed contracts that need dedicated capacity: one disclosed in April 2024 (an analyst on the May-2026 call recalled a January-2027 start), a May-2025 agreement for advanced intermediates with a "major global pharmaceutical company" (₹650-750 cr of capex funded by the customer's capacity-reservation advance) and a third. Together they cost ~₹2,000 cr, ~70% is capitalised, validations are complete and validation batches have shipped; they are "three different products completely" (CEO, 1-Aug-2026). Commercial volumes start only after each customer files Divi's into its drug application and regulators approve, which management says can take six months to three years ("to be optimistic... the 2-year range"). The money is visible on the balance sheet: customers advanced ₹1,207 cr in FY26 (₹496 cr in FY25), including a ₹456 cr refundable advance and ₹402 cr of deferred capacity-reservation revenue.

blocks.h: Peptides and GLP-1: real capability, little disclosure

blocks.p: Divi's has made protected amino acids (the building blocks of peptides) for ~20 years. It has added a large pilot plant, several 3,000-litre solid-phase (SPPS) reactors, more being installed, and liquid-phase capacity, and opened a Peptide Centre of Excellence in FY26. It says it is the only maker integrated from basic raw materials through protected amino acids to fragments, and wants to be "the largest integrated player". Several fragments have been validated and supplied; customers are in Phase I-III. Management will not say whether any of this is GLP-1 ("I cannot answer that question", 1-Aug-2026). Citi (15-Jul-2026) expects GLP-1 API supplies from FY27 and links Divi's to Merck's enlicitide and J&J's icotrokinra (oral peptides) from CY2027; those are Citi's attributions, not the company's.

Divi's already supplies iodine-based contrast agents (used in CT scans) to innovators in "several multiples of tons". On 1-Aug-2026 the CEO said long-term contracts with two customers are being signed, one already commercial and the second starting "in the next few months", in "substantial quantities". Gadolinium agents (for MRI) remain with a customer in Phase II/III trials.

blocks.callout: **Our view:** the dedicated projects are the most credible growth Divi's has had since Covid: customers are paying upfront and validations are done. But the timing belongs to customers and regulators, and Divi's discloses neither product nor size. We model CS +26.5% / +22.2% / +18.4% (FY27-29E), taking it to 64% of revenue; a year's slip in approvals is our bear case.

sections.title: Generic APIs: world-scale and lowest-cost, but in a price war; volumes hold, value does not grow

blocks.p: Divi's makes ~30 large-volume generic APIs and is the world's largest maker of 10 of them, with 60-70% shares in several (CEO, Aug-2025). Generic API revenue (ex-nutraceuticals) was ₹3,045 cr in FY22, ₹3,700 cr in FY23 and has been flat since: ₹3,759 cr in FY25 and ₹3,806 cr in FY26 (+1%), +6% in Q1FY27. Management says volumes are stable and no customer has been lost; the problem is price, as Chinese producers and squeezed generic formulators push it down. Recent price rises only pass on solvent costs: "It's not based on the markets have corrected and the pricing pressure has gone down" (CEO, 1-Aug-2026). Most generic volume is on long-term contracts with raw-material clauses, with some spot sales in South America, Eastern Europe and Asia.

pair.title: Generic API revenue: flat at ~₹3,600-3,800 cr for four years

pair.title: Named products: valsartan shrinking
pair.source: AR FY25 and FY26, business responsibility report (life-cycle assessments)

blocks.p: **New products help at the margin.** Divi's has filed four new DMFs (drug master files) for APIs coming off patent, naming brivaracetam and ticagrelor; validation quantities are with customers and commercial volumes are expected within 3-6 months, and one customer wants long-term exclusivity. Kakinada lets Divi's make more of its own starting materials, which is how it held share through the price war. Against a ₹3,800 cr base, four launches add a few points of growth, not a new leg.

blocks.callout: **Our view:** generics are a cash-generating, low-growth business that Divi's runs for volume, scale and customer loyalty. We model +8% in FY27 (currency and launches) and +6% a year after. The risk is not share loss but continued price erosion; the upside would be a market correction as high-cost producers exit, which management says has not started.

sections.title: Nutraceuticals: a steady carotenoid business growing ~20%, now 9-10% of revenue

blocks.p: Divi's has made carotenoids at Unit 2 since 2007: astaxanthin, beta-carotene, lycopene, canthaxanthin and apocarotenal, plus vitamins A, D2, D3, E and K2, sold to food, supplement and animal-feed makers as powders, beadlets and liquids. Revenue rose from ₹629 cr (FY22) to ₹781 cr (FY25) and ₹946 cr (FY26, +21%); Q1FY27 was ₹298 cr (+19%). Covid hurt multivitamin demand; it has recovered steadily, and capacity is being added "as and when required".

exhibit.title: Nutraceutical revenue: +21% in FY26, +19% in Q1FY27
exhibit.source: Earnings calls; GAM estimates FY27-29E

blocks.callout: **Our view:** a good niche (few large carotenoid makers outside Europe and China) but too small to move the valuation. We model +18% / +12% / +10%.

sections.title: Capacity: ~₹5,400 cr of capex in four years has pushed asset turns to a low; the payback depends on the projects above

blocks.p: Divi's spent ₹1,003 cr (FY24), ₹1,438 cr (FY25) and ₹2,520 cr (FY26) on capex, 23.9% of FY26 sales against an FY16-25 average of ~12%. Gross block rose from ₹6,365 cr (Mar-23) to ₹9,413 cr (Mar-26), with ₹2,034 cr more in capital work in progress at Jun-26. The spend has three parts: the dedicated CS projects (~₹2,000 cr), Kakinada (a ₹1,500 cr first phase, ₹600 cr capitalised; six blocks running, two under construction; a second phase of four blocks under evaluation) and peptide capacity. Utilisation is ~80-85% across the three units (1-Aug-2026). Revenue per rupee of gross block fell from 1.5x (FY21) to 1.1x (FY26); management aims to get back towards 1.5-1.8x over 4-5 years.

pair.title: Capex vs depreciation: building far ahead of wear and tear
Asset turn at a decade low

blocks.callout: **Our view:** Divi's has historically built capacity about two years ahead of revenue and then filled it, and the customer prepayments say this round is wanted. But we are at the expensive point of the cycle: depreciation rises from ₹463 cr to ~₹773 cr by FY29E, and free cash flow stays thin until the projects ramp. We model capex of ₹2,000 / 2,000 / 1,800 cr and no big new project; a Kakinada Phase 2 approval would add to it.

sections.title: Competitive advantage: a real moat in process chemistry, reliability and customer trust; no pricing power in generics

blocks.p: A moat is a lasting advantage that lets a company earn more than its cost of capital for longer than rivals. Divi's has one, but of a particular kind: it is the lowest-cost, most reliable supplier for chemistry it chooses to do, and innovators trust it with their filings. That shows up in decades-long customer relationships, prepaid capacity and a 12-29% ROE through the cycle, not in the ability to raise prices.

blocks.callout: **Verdict:** a genuine but narrow moat. Process cost and regulatory reliability are hard to copy and explain why big pharma keeps coming back; switching costs exist only for the life of each molecule; generic APIs have no pricing power; peptides are a capability, not yet an advantage. Indian rivals (Laurus, Neuland, Sai Life, Piramal Pharma, Cohance) and Chinese CDMOs compete for the same projects. We would pay a premium for the franchise, but not an unlimited one.

sections.title: No real seasonality, but lumpy: custom-synthesis shipments move margins by 3-6 points from one quarter to the next

blocks.p: Divi's sells bulk APIs and intermediates on customers' delivery schedules, so quarters swing with shipment timing rather than with a season. In FY25-26 the EBITDA margin moved between 29% and 34%, highest when custom synthesis was a bigger share. Q1FY27 broke the range: revenue +27.8% to ₹3,080 cr, gross margin 68% and EBITDA margin 40.7%, as validation batches of the three dedicated projects shipped, the rupee was far weaker than a year earlier (standalone growth was ~10% in constant currency) and inventory rose by ~₹500 cr. Management asked investors to judge margins by the year, not the quarter (Nilima Divi, 1-Aug-2026).

pair.title: Quarterly revenue: a step up in Q1FY27
Quarterly EBITDA margin: 29-34% for two years, then 41%

blocks.callout: **What to watch:** whether the Q2FY27 gross margin stays above ~60% once the three-month raw-material stockpile (bought at high solvent prices) is consumed, and whether custom synthesis stays near 60% of revenue without validation batches. Q2FY27 results are due by mid-November 2026.

sections.title: Three acts: steady compounding to FY20, a Covid windfall in FY21-22, a two-year hangover, and a recovery that is now running ahead of the old peak

blocks.p: Divi's grew revenue from ₹3,115 cr in FY15 to ₹5,394 cr in FY20 (~12% a year) at 33-38% EBITDA margins. Covid then turned a steady compounder into a boom-and-bust: revenue jumped 29% in each of FY21 and FY22 to ₹8,960 cr, the margin hit 43% and EPS reached ₹111.5, helped by emergency supplies such as the API for Merck's molnupiravir. When those orders stopped in FY23 and generic API prices fell, revenue dropped 13%, the margin fell to 28% (FY24) and EPS sank to ₹60.3. The recovery since has been real: revenue +19% in FY25 and +13% in FY26 to ₹10,560 cr, EPS ₹96.7, and Q1FY27 EPS of ₹34.0 puts the trailing twelve months at ~₹110, near the Covid peak. But the margin (32.6% in FY26) is still below the pre-Covid 33-38% band, and part of the recent growth is the weak rupee.

blocks.callout: **Our view:** strip out the Covid years and Divi's has compounded EPS at ~8-9% a year over a decade (₹42 in FY16 to ₹97 in FY26), with an ROE that has fallen from the mid-20s to the mid-teens as the balance sheet filled with cash, inventory and new plants. The next leg depends on custom-synthesis projects that are built and validated but not yet commercial. The history says Divi's executes; it also says one-off demand can flatter a year badly, which is why we treat Q1FY27 with care.

sections.title: Margins: Q1FY27's 41% came from inventory, mix and the rupee; we model 35.5% for FY27, still above management's "similar to last year"

blocks.p: Divi's gross margin (revenue less materials) ran at 59-66% for a decade; the EBITDA margin at 28-43%. The FY23-24 fall came from lost Covid volumes, generic price erosion and expensive raw materials; FY25-26 recovered to ~32-33% as custom synthesis grew. Q1FY27 jumped to a 68% gross and 40.7% EBITDA margin. Three things drove it: (1) a ~₹500 cr rise in inventory booked through the P&L, from a rolling three-month raw-material stockpile bought at war-inflated solvent prices and validation-batch work in progress (an analyst estimated the gross margin at 55-58% without it; management says no inventory gain was booked); (2) mix, with custom synthesis at 60%; and (3) the rupee.

pair.title: Annual margins: Q1FY27 is far above the recent band
Cost lines, % of revenue: materials fell, people and overheads did not
pair.source: Screener.in expense schedules; PL Q1FY27 note

blocks.h: How much does the rupee add?

blocks.p: Exports are ~89% of revenue, while imports are ~40% of a ₹4,000-5,000 cr raw-material bill (CFO, 23-May-2026). On FY26's cost structure, a 10% weaker rupee would lift rupee revenue by ~9% and costs by only ~1.6% of sales, adding roughly 4 points to the EBITDA margin before hedges and price pass-through (GAM illustration). That is why FY26's margin edged up with a ~6% currency tailwind (12.8% reported growth vs 6.8% constant currency) and why Q1FY27 looked so strong. It works in reverse if the rupee recovers.

blocks.p: Price Waterhouse audits Divi's; there are no qualifications, no debt and small related-party dealings. Cash conversion is decent over time (operating cash flow ₹2,738 cr in FY26, 80% of EBITDA) but swings with inventory. FY26 brought new accounting that investors should understand, because it moves revenue between years.

sections.title: No debt and ₹3,400-3,600 cr of cash, but working capital ties up ~44% of sales and capex has absorbed the free cash flow

blocks.p: Divi's has no borrowings (₹7 cr of leases at Mar-2026). Cash and bank deposits fell from ₹4,213 cr (Mar-2023) to ₹3,414 cr (Mar-2026) because capex (₹2,520 cr in FY26, 24% of sales) and the ₹797 cr dividend took everything the business produced: free cash flow on Screener's basis was only ₹215-258 cr a year in FY24-26. Working capital is the other drain. Inventory is ~346 days of material cost (Screener) and reached ₹4,413 cr at Jun-2026 after the three-month stockpile; receivables are ~100 days. Customers now fund part of the build: Divi's received ₹1,207 cr of advances in FY26, including a ₹456 cr interest-free refundable advance and ₹402 cr of capacity-reservation payments released to revenue over the contract (AR FY26 notes 14-16).

blocks.callout: **Cash in the model:** the forecast "cash & investments" row is net of borrowings (₹3,476 cr at Mar-2026). With ₹5,800 cr of capex over FY27-29E and working capital growing with sales, we expect it to rise only to about {{F.treasury.2|num}} cr by Mar-2029. Customer advances sit inside "other liabilities", so the model treats them as working capital, not debt; if a project were cancelled, the ₹456 cr refundable advance would have to be repaid.

sections.title: Capital allocation: no debt, no acquisitions, no dilution, a flat ₹30 dividend, and returns that have halved from the peak while the plants are built

blocks.p: Divi's has never bought a company and has not issued shares since the FY16 bonus. It reinvests most of its cash in plants and pays a fixed ₹30 a share (~₹797 cr, 31% of FY26 profit; yield ~0.3% at ₹9,292). ROE fell from 28% (FY22) to 12% (FY24) and recovered to 16% (FY26); return on operating capital (excluding cash) from 40% to 22%. Cash of ~₹3,400 cr earns ~7-8% and dilutes ROE by ~2 points. We forecast ROE of {{F.roe.0|pct}} / {{F.roe.1|pct}} / {{F.roe.2|pct}}: comfortably above the 11.6% cost of equity, far below the 28% of FY22.

pair.title: Returns: below the peak, above the cost of capital
Where the cash went in FY24-26

blocks.callout: **Our view:** disciplined and conservative: organic growth, no leverage, no empire-building. The cost is a lazy balance sheet and a dividend that has not grown in five years. With capex running at 15-24% of sales, cash will not build much until the projects pay back; we do not expect a buyback or special dividend.

sections.title: Ownership: the Divi family 52%, foreign funds 20%, domestic institutions 19%

blocks.p: The Divi family owns 51.88% (Jun-2026). Dr. Kiran S. Divi (CEO) and Ms. Nilima Prasad Divi (commercial head), the founder's children, hold 20.34% each; Mrs. Swarnalatha Divi 5.27%, Divi's Biotech 3.01% and Dr. Murali K. Divi 2.85% (Mar-2026). Nothing is pledged. Foreign funds own 20.19% (up from ~15% in early 2024) and domestic institutions 19.29%, of which mutual funds 13.87%; LIC cut its stake from 5.63% to 2.79% in FY26. The number of shareholders fell from 3.5 lakh (Dec-2023) to 2,26,324.

sections.title: Management and governance: a founder-led family firm with a clear succession and a clean record, but promoter pay of ₹224 cr is excessive

blocks.p: Dr. Murali K. Divi founded the company in 1990 and is still Managing Director (re-appointed from Oct-2024 for five years). The next generation is already running it: Dr. Kiran S. Divi is CEO (re-appointed from April 2025) and leads customers, technology and peptides on calls; Ms. Nilima Prasad Divi heads commercial and presents the financials. Long-serving N. V. Ramana (Executive Director since 1994) and Dr. S. Devendra Rao (manufacturing, since 2024) complete the executive side. Five of ten directors are independent and the chairman, Dr. Ramesh B. V. Nimmagadda, is independent. The CFO changed in August 2025 for the first time in decades, when L. Kishore Babu retired and V. P. Pasumarthy took over.

blocks.callout: **Where we could be wrong:** our FY26-29E EPS growth (~17.8% a year) is double Divi's ~8.6% of FY16-26. Upside risk: the dedicated projects and peptide fragments ramp faster, the Q1 margin proves sticky, and the rupee stays weak, which is close to our bull case (FY28E EPS ₹{{scen.bull.eps.1|n1}}). sections.title: The street: 7 Buy, 4 Hold, 1 Sell after Q1FY27; median target ₹9,106, below the ₹9,292 price

blocks.p: We found 12 notes dated 31-Jul to 4-Aug-2026, after Q1FY27. Citi is highest (Buy, ₹11,700; GLP-1 and complex oral peptides from CY27), then Jefferies and Macquarie (₹10,200), JM Financial (₹9,510, 41x FY28E EV/EBITDA), HDFC Securities (₹9,230, 39x Q1FY29E EV/EBITDA, "56.5x P/E"), Morgan Stanley (₹9,111) and JPMorgan (₹9,100). The cautious end: PL Accumulate ₹8,600, DRChoksey Hold ₹8,521, Systematix Hold ₹7,959, Motilal Oswal Neutral ₹7,720 (55x 12-month forward EPS: "limited upside from current valuations") and ICICI Securities, which downgraded to Sell at ₹6,500. The average is ~₹9,029 and the median ₹9,106; the stock then rose another ~10-15% in August-September to ₹9,292. Pre-results calls still standing include BOBCAPS Hold ₹7,500 (56x Mar-28E), Ambit Sell ₹6,230 and Kotak Sell ₹5,850. We found no September notes.

Its margins and ROE are among the best of the CDMOs, which justifies a premium; it does not tell us the premium should keep widening.

sections.title: Our honest summary: own the business, not the price

blocks.callout: **What you are buying:** India's best-run API and custom-synthesis platform: world-scale, lowest-cost chemistry, 12 of the top 20 pharma companies as customers, three customer-funded dedicated projects about to commercialise, a credible peptide and contrast-media pipeline, no debt and a clean regulatory record. Earnings should grow ~18% a year to FY29E on our numbers.

**What you are paying:** 78.7x our FY27E and 67.8x FY28E EPS, after a ~38% rise in three months. Our 59x Sep-28E multiple is Divi's own 2021-26 median (55.9x) lifted 5.4% for a sector trading above its history, and it gives {{dcf.tp|inr}} ({{dcf.upside|chg}}). The DCF (₹2,872) says the cash flows support far less. The price already assumes the pipeline arrives on time and at scale.

blocks.p: **Is it a SELL on the business?** No. Our call is about price, not quality: we expect earnings to grow strongly, and our base case already assumes custom synthesis rises to ~64% of sales. The stock is a SELL because the rule compares the price with a target built from the multiple the market has paid for Divi's over five years, and the price now sits above it. A strong Q2, a contract announcement or a GLP-1 confirmation could keep the stock above our target for a while; we would revisit the multiple only if the evidence of faster growth became public, not on price momentum.

sections.title: Glossary

exhibit.title: Terms used in this report
head: Term
What it means
rows: Active pharmaceutical ingredient: the chemical in a medicine that has the effect; Divi's sells APIs to companies that make the tablets.
Chemicals made on the way to an API; "advanced intermediates" are the last steps before it.
Making an innovator's molecule to its specification under contract; CDMO = contract development and manufacturing organisation.
An API for a drug whose patents have expired, sold to many generic drug makers.
Drug master file (US) and certificate of suitability (Europe): regulatory dossiers that let customers use Divi's API.
The chemistry, manufacturing and controls part of a drug application; once Divi's is named there, switching supplier needs re-approval.
Production batches that prove a process works at scale before commercial supply.
Peptides are short chains of amino acids (GLP-1 drugs are peptides); SPPS and LPPS are solid- and liquid-phase ways of making them.
A class of diabetes and obesity drugs (e.g. semaglutide, tirzepatide), mostly peptides.
Agents injected for CT (iodine-based) or MRI (gadolinium-based) scans.
Revenue growth with exchange rates held at last year's level.
Revenue less materials; operating profit before depreciation, interest, tax and other income, as % of revenue.
Share price ÷ next full year's EPS; enterprise value (market value less net cash) ÷ EBITDA.
Half FY28E plus half FY29E: the earnings the market will look at in twelve months.
House rule: the stock's median forward P/E since Apr-2021 (trough years left out), multiplied by how far sector peers trade above or below their five-year median P/E.
Discounted cash flow value; the return shareholders require (here 11.6%).
Dates whose forward EPS is a loss or below half the prior three-year peak are left out of the median.
